findings.claim: This change removes 'on the default branch' from the tree-ambiguity rule in the closure reference, but two other places still state the scoped rule. The living actuals spec (openspec/specs/actuals-instrumentation/spec.md:118) still reads 'more than one commit on the default branch carries it'. The anchor regression test still describes the rule that way (engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_d2_anchor_test.go:37-40) and implements it as 'reachable from ref' (resolveTreeToCommitOrAmbiguous, lines 404-419). The closure contract and the authoritative spec plus its pinned regression now disagree on which carriers make an anchor ambiguous. A tree carried by one default-branch commit and by one commit on another ref is ambiguous under the reference but resolvable under the spec and the test. The new requireClauses/rejectClauses pin protects the divergence instead of catching it. Every omission this produces is conservative: t1 is omitted, never wrong.

With the branch scope removed, 'more than one commit carries it' no longer says which commit set is searched: one branch, all local refs, remote-tracking refs, or unreachable objects. Closure is the only actuals writer and writes each record once. Two closures of the same change in clones with different refs, such as a fetched feature branch whose squash reproduces the tree, can therefore reach different verified-or-omitted t1 verdicts. A stored measurement becomes dependent on the environment.

The rewritten bullet still starts with 'If a tree hash is all that is available' and makes only the more-than-one case ambiguous. It therefore implies that a single carrier found by tree search may become the anchor. That is discovery by tree, which the bullet at line 37 forbids ('MUST be used to verify a commit, never to discover one'). The commit kept this contradiction in a line it rewrote.
